T03 can now complete R4 on its own; listing in the queue belongs to the queue's tasks (T09, T21), and a queue in cma run's terminal review is written down as out of scope.
C1 now states what the fifth T03 review found open: a payment rail with cash wording is ambiguous whatever other cue matches, words match whole in any script (CAFÉSTRIPE is not STRIPE), and a declared category order, not rule order, picks the category inside a bucket.
Every other requirement, property and id is unchanged; the consumer trace adds the conflict string's readers, the word-boundary helper and the same-bucket categories, found with git grep on the T03 branch (ecec4ca).
One owner question: the category order inside a bucket (default: more checks first, so a gateway payout with an invoice reference goes through the round-trip check).

questions.context: Category inside one bucket (design C1 step 6, revision 4). Two rules can agree on the bucket but carry different categories: FPS CREDIT STRIPE INV 17 matches a gateway (card settlement) and an invoice reference (customer transfer); RETURNED DD REFUND, with no bank code at the start, matches a returned-payment cue and a refund cue. Today rule order picks, and the fifth T03 review showed that reordering rules can move a credit out of M2, because the round-trip check reads only customer transfers. M7, M15 and the M16 numerator also read these categories. The design fixes an order in the table that puts first the category with more checks. The cost: such a gateway payout counts as a named customer in M15, and such a refund counts in M7 as a returned direct debit.
options: More checks first: cash deposit, then customer transfer, then card settlement; returned payment before refund (design default)
Named processor first: cash deposit, then card settlement, then customer transfer; refund before returned payment
Same bucket with different categories is ambiguous too (amends R4's bucket test and adds to the queue)

proposals.text: T03 (re-open on revision 4; blocked at 5 of 5): R4 only, no judgement queue. The verdict in C1's order: longer-phrase filter; the bank's code at the start settles alone; a payment rail with cash paid-in wording is ambiguous before any cue decides; then cues with a bucket, then names; inside the bucket, the table's declared category order; an ambiguous credit records v2:conflict: with every match from both stages, the rail included, in table order. Whole-word matching in any script for rule names and profile names (one definition). The production caller is cma run under CMA_RULESET=v2, which writes each line's rule into the evidence lines. Tests (contracts): the four verify-32 cases (BACS CREDIT HMRC CASH PAID IN ambiguous with rail, HMRC and cash; FPS CREDIT HMRC TO SAVINGS STRIPE with savings, HMRC, rail and gateway; FPS CREDIT CAFÉSTRIPE LTD unexplained by default; COUNTER DEPOSIT GRANT ST BRANCH ambiguous with its candidates in cma run's evidence lines), each asserting category and candidate set.

T09 and T21 (R15): the queue entry for an ambiguous credit carries its candidates, each with the category its rule sets and the bucket that category maps to, looked up in the ruleset named before the first colon of the line's rule; a rail candidate shows as giving no bucket. Test: an ambiguous credit is listed by amount among unexplained lines, and FPS CREDIT HMRC TO SAVINGS STRIPE shows HMRC repayments, own-account transfers, trading receipts and no bucket.
T08 (R14): the irregular-acquirer indicator reads the acquirer and gateway name lists, not the category, so a gateway payout that the category order made a customer transfer is still checked.

Rule-order shuffle over whole statements (contracts, in T03): for several seeds, shuffle the rules within each v2 stage, run categorise on every committed fixture, the pairwise matrix and a two-line FPS DEBIT STRIPE / FPS CREDIT STRIPE INV 17 statement, and assert identical categories, candidate sets and M2, M7 and M15; only the recorded rule among same-category matches and the written order of candidates may change.

Ambiguity invariant (contracts, in T04): for every credit whose rule has the conflict form, its id is in M25's evidence and in neither M2's nor M18's, and its candidate set equals every rule it matches in either stage after the longer-phrase filter.

2026-11-18 Put each clause on the requirement whose task builds the component it needs: R4 asking the categoriser task to list lines in the workspace's judgement queue failed T03's review until the clause moved to R15 (D58, D60).
2026-11-18 Word boundaries in rule patterns must treat letters and digits in any script as word characters; an ASCII-only boundary let STRIPE inside CAFÉSTRIPE count as trading receipts (verify-32).

# Requirements — Statement review: every figure traced, the unclear lines first

Bet: statement-review, signed 2026-11-16. Scope is a showcase for one firm (D15, D24): a working model the underwriter can try, after which the firm's approver decides on a pilot (D14, D25). Forms and risk tags follow the template.

Revision 4, after D60 (changes requested; the owner raised it as D58 after the fifth T03 review). R4's queue clause moves to R15, so that each task can complete its own requirement. R4 marks an ambiguous credit as ambiguous, places it in unexplained money in, and records as its candidates every rule it matched in either stage. R15's judgement queue, which already lists every unexplained line, shows each ambiguous credit's candidates and the bucket each would give. One term, candidates, is defined below. Every other requirement, property and id is as revision 3 left it.

Revision 3, after D52 (changes requested; the owner raised it as D49 after the fourth T03 review). Only R4 changes: it gains the ambiguity policy, and the two terms it uses are defined below. Every other requirement, property and id is as revision 2 left it.

Revision 2, after D34 (changes requested). Ids from revision 1 are kept and never reused. Changed: R1 and R14 (cash deposits are trading receipts and the large ones are flagged, D31); R15 (judgement queue); R22, R23, R26 and R28 (the pack is written once, at sign-off, and carries the policy check); R25 (pass/refer/fail shown with the illustrative label, D28); R47 (synthetic cash); R50 (no durations, D32); P1 and P17. New: R55, R56, P19, P20. Withdrawn: R49 (timing the underwriter, D32). Confirmed as designed: local-first (D29), OBIE v3.1 and TrueLayer first (D30), Tier 1 only by 2026-11-29 (D33).

Terms. *The system*: the cma package running on the underwriter's machine. *Figures layer*: src/cma/metrics.py and a new indicators module, the only code that does arithmetic on money (ADR 001). *Case*: one application, holding one or more of the applicant's accounts, a profile, an override log and a case log. *The reply*: the underwriter's written answers of 2026-11-16 (one anecdotal source; see evidence-synthesis.md). *Judgement queue*: the lines the workspace lists first because a person has to decide what they are. *Policy check*: the pass, refer or fail outcome and the rule results from the packaged policy (src/cma/policies/uk_sme_default.yaml). Its rule ids (R1 to R9, cited as [R1] to [R9] in a pack) are not the requirement ids in this file. *Illustrative label*: the sentence shown with every policy outcome, saying that the thresholds ship with the tool, are not the firm's lending policy, and do not make the lending decision. *Preview*: the pack's content and its snapshot hash, shown before sign-off; nothing is written until sign-off. *Line-type cue* (revision 3): wording that says what kind of line it is: a returned payment, a move to or from the applicant's own pot or savings, HMRC, a refund or reversal, or the payment rail (Faster Payment, BACS, CHAPS, a transfer, a standing order), which belongs to no bucket. *Name list* (revision 3): a maintained list of who sent a credit or what it is for: acquirers, gateways, marketplaces, delivery platforms, lenders and merchant cash advance providers, director and capital-introduced wording, cash paid-in wording, invoice references and explained non-trading words. *Candidates* (revision 4): every rule an ambiguous credit matched in either stage, that is among its line-type cues and among the name lists, counting a match inside a longer listed phrase only as the longer phrase. A payment-rail cue can be a candidate; it gives no bucket.

## R1 · ubiquitous · risk: money
THE SYSTEM SHALL place every credit in a case in exactly one money-in bucket (trading receipts, own-account transfers in, director and shareholder funding, lending drawdowns, refunds and returned payments, HMRC repayments, other explained money in, unexplained), and SHALL report total money in and each bucket as a GBP figure with the ids of the lines behind it.
Source: the reply, 'if a tool could reliably tell me that £80k entered the business account but only £55k represented genuine trading receipts, explain the remaining £25k'; D31 (cash deposits sit inside trading receipts, R55).

## R2 · ubiquitous · risk: money
THE SYSTEM SHALL compute every money figure, bucket, monthly cell, indicator comparison and comparison difference in integer pence from GBP amounts, in the figures layer only, and never in the review workspace, the pack renderer or a model.

## R3 · unwanted · risk: money
IF the money-in buckets do not sum to total money in to the penny, or any credit is in no bucket or in more than one, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT show or export figures for the case, and SHALL report the difference in pence and the lines involved.

## R4 · ubiquitous · risk: money
THE SYSTEM SHALL recognise, from maintained lists shipped as data: credits from UK card acquirers, payment gateways, marketplaces and delivery platforms as trading receipts; lines naming UK business lenders and merchant cash advance providers as lending drawdowns (money in) or debt service (money out); moves between the applicant's own pots or savings as own-account transfers; HMRC credits as HMRC repayments; refund and reversal credits as refunds; and cash paid in at a counter or machine as cash deposits.
THE SYSTEM SHALL treat a credit's wording as ambiguous when its line-type cues point to more than one money-in bucket, when a payment rail appears with cash paid-in wording, or, with no line-type cue, when the name lists it matches point to more than one money-in bucket; SHALL mark an ambiguous credit as ambiguous, place it in unexplained money in, and record as its candidates every rule it matched in either stage; and SHALL NOT count it as trading receipts unless the underwriter moves it there with an override (R17). Only a per-line override (R17), a case-profile name (R5, R6) or an own-account pairing (R8) settles an ambiguous credit; a firm rule does not. Line-type cues that agree outrank name lists that point elsewhere (PAYPAL REFUND is a refund); a returned-payment code the bank prints at the start of the line (UNPAID DD) settles the line type on its own; and a match inside a longer listed phrase counts only as the longer phrase (STRIPE CAPITAL is a lending drawdown, not also a card settlement; HMRC REFUND is an HMRC repayment).
Source: README known limits (unknown acquirers land in M16); the reply (Stripe, SumUp, merchant cash advances); D46 (line-type wording before name lists); D48 (bare words are not evidence); D52 (ambiguous or conflicting wording goes to the judgement queue and is never counted as trading receipts); D58 and D60 (R4 marks the credit and records its candidates; the judgement queue that lists it is R15's).

## R5 · conditional · risk: money
IF the case profile names a director or shareholder, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL put each credit whose counterparty matches that name in director and shareholder funding, even when the credit carries an invoice reference.

## R6 · conditional · risk: money
IF the case profile names the applicant's other accounts, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL classify lines in either direction whose counterparty matches one of them as own-account transfers, and SHALL leave them out of trading receipts and out of operating cash flow (M9).

## R7 · unwanted · risk: money
IF no built-in rule, firm rule or override explains a credit, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT count it as trading receipts; it stays in unexplained money in.

## R8 · conditional · risk: money
IF a case holds more than one of the applicant's accounts, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL pair each debit in one account with the single credit of the same amount in another account of the case within the configured number of days, and SHALL classify both lines as own-account transfers.
Source: the reply, 'transfers between business accounts can inflate turnover if counted twice'.

## R9 · unwanted · risk: money
IF a debit has more than one candidate credit for an own-account pairing, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT pair it, and SHALL list the debit and every candidate in the judgement queue as a possible own-account transfer.

## R10 · ubiquitous · risk: money
THE SYSTEM SHALL keep the ids, units and values of M1 to M16 unchanged on every committed synthetic case and test fixture, except for lines that a new rule now recognises, which the change SHALL list; M16 SHALL be renamed so that its name says it measures money in that is not trading receipts.

## R11 · ubiquitous · risk: money
THE SYSTEM SHALL produce a monthly summary with one row per calendar month in the period, part months marked as part, giving money in, money out, trading receipts, average end-of-day balance, lowest end-of-day balance and days overdrawn, each cell with the ids of the lines behind it.
Source: the reply, 'calculating monthly credits, debits, average balances and existing repayments'.

## R12 · ubiquitous · risk: money
THE SYSTEM SHALL report the average end-of-day balance over the period as a figure, citing the lines that set each day's closing balance.

## R13 · conditional · risk: money
IF the case profile gives the proposed facility's monthly repayment, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL report debt service cover including that repayment; otherwise THE SYSTEM SHALL show that figure as n/a with the reason.

## R14 · ubiquitous · risk: data
THE SYSTEM SHALL raise risk indicators from thresholds in an editable file (a single credit that is large against typical trading receipts; each cash deposit at or above the single-deposit limit; a calendar month in which cash deposits exceed a set share of that month's trading receipts; a cash deposit made within a set number of days after a cash withdrawal of an amount within a set tolerance; payments to gambling operators; returned direct debits; runs of consecutive overdrawn days; irregular credits from a named acquirer), each listing its lines and the threshold that fired, and SHALL label any threshold still at its shipped value as illustrative.
Source: the reply, 'Highlight director loans, unusual credits and large cash deposits'; 'Flag returned direct debits, persistent overdraft usage'; D31, 'with deposits above a threshold flagged'.

## R15 · event · risk: ux
WHEN the underwriter opens a case, THE SYSTEM SHALL show the money-in breakdown, the monthly summary, the figures, the indicators and, while R25 applies, the policy check, with the judgement queue (unexplained lines, ambiguous credits among them, possible own-account transfers, and every line an indicator flagged, which includes cash deposits at or above the single-deposit limit) listed first, largest amount first, and SHALL show for each ambiguous credit in the queue its candidates (R4) and the money-in bucket each would give.
Source: D58 and D60 (the queue clause moved here from R4).

## R16 · event · risk: ux
WHEN the underwriter selects a figure, a bucket or a monthly cell, THE SYSTEM SHALL list exactly the lines behind it, each with date, description, amount, balance, category and the rule or override that set the category; for a sum it SHALL show the lines' total next to the figure, and for an average, share, ratio or count it SHALL show the inputs and the method.
Source: the reply, 'I'd want to click any number in the report and see exactly which transactions make up that figure'.

## R17 · event · risk: money
WHEN the underwriter changes a line's category and gives a reason, THE SYSTEM SHALL append the change (line, old and new category, reason, typed name, operating-system user, UTC time) to the case's override log, recompute every figure from the statements and the whole override log, and mark each figure that now rests on an overridden line.
Source: the reply, 'Allow me to manually correct categories'.

## R18 · unwanted · risk: money
IF a requested change would alter a line's amount, date, balance or description, add or remove a line, or give a line a category not valid for its direction, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT accept it; overrides change categories only.

## R19 · conditional · risk: data
IF an override names a line that is not in the case, or was recorded against a statement file whose hash no longer matches, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT apply it, and SHALL show it as stale until the underwriter confirms or drops it.

## R20 · event · risk: data
WHEN the underwriter promotes an override to a firm rule, THE SYSTEM SHALL show the lines the rule would match in the open case before saving, then save the counterparty pattern, direction, category, name, time and reason to the firm rules file, and apply the rule to every case categorised afterwards.

## R21 · unwanted · risk: money
IF a firm rule would reclassify a line matched by a built-in director, capital, shareholder, lender, HMRC or returned-payment pattern, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT apply the firm rule to that line; only a per-line override with a reason can change it.

## R22 · event · risk: data
WHEN the underwriter signs off a case's figures, THE SYSTEM SHALL require a typed name, record it with the operating-system user and UTC time, and bind it to the snapshot of the preview the underwriter signed: statement hashes, ruleset, firm rules, profile, override log position, thresholds, memo field map, policy hash, the show_policy_verdict setting and package version.

## R23 · unwanted · risk: data
IF anything in the snapshot has changed since the preview was built, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT accept the sign-off, and SHALL say what changed.

## R24 · ubiquitous · risk: ux
THE SYSTEM SHALL word the underwriter's action as signing off the figures, never as approving the loan, and SHALL leave the recommendation and every judgement field blank for the underwriter.
Source: the reply, 'I wouldn't want AI making the final lending decision. I'd want it assisting the underwriter.'

## R25 · state · risk: ux
WHILE show_policy_verdict is on in the firm configuration (the default), THE SYSTEM SHALL show in the review workspace and the pack the overall pass, refer or fail outcome and each rule's result from the packaged policy, computed from the current figures, and SHALL put the illustrative label in the same workspace panel and the same pack section as the outcome.
Source: D28, 'Show it, labelled as illustrative thresholds, not the firm's policy'; README:127, 'Policy thresholds are illustrative. They are not any lender's real policy.'

## R26 · event · risk: data
WHEN a case is signed off, THE SYSTEM SHALL write the review pack once, from the signed preview, containing: memo-ready sections ordered by an editable memo field map (by default the 13 fields listed in the reply), each figure followed by its id; while R25 applies, a policy-check section after the memo fields that no memo field maps to; a self-contained HTML record that works offline, with click-through from every figure to its lines and the sign-off; the evidence JSON; and the monthly summary as CSV. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT overwrite an existing pack.
Source: the reply, 'Produce a summary I can use directly in my credit memo'.

## R27 · conditional · risk: data
IF a memo field has no figure mapped to it, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL mark it as for the underwriter and leave it empty.

## R28 · unwanted · risk: data
IF the pack's text fails the grounding guard (a number that is not a figure or a policy threshold at the precision shown, a figure without its id, or a threshold without its rule id and a limit word), THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT write the pack.

## R29 · state · risk: security
WHILE offline lock is on in the firm configuration (the default), THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse to create a hosted model client, SHALL refuse to start the MCP server, SHALL open no network connection other than the loopback workspace, and SHALL record offline mode in every evidence record.
Source: the reply, 'A tool that operates entirely on our own machine or within our own environment, without transmitting customer data externally, could be attractive.'

## R30 · unwanted · risk: security
IF a hosted model is used, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT put transaction descriptions, counterparty names, case profile fields or any line-level data in a prompt; a prompt carries only the metric and rule tables, the period and the placeholder account name.

## R31 · ubiquitous · risk: security
THE SYSTEM SHALL keep each case's statements, profile, logs and outputs under one case root readable only by the operating-system user who created it, and SHALL refuse to create a case root inside a git working tree that does not ignore it.

## R32 · conditional · risk: security
IF the case root lies inside a folder that a known cloud-sync client uploads (OneDrive, Dropbox, Google Drive, iCloud Drive), THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL warn before creating a case, and SHALL record the warning in the case log.

## R33 · event · risk: security
WHEN the review workspace starts, THE SYSTEM SHALL listen on the loopback interface only, issue a new random session token, refuse any request that lacks the token or carries a Host header other than the loopback address and port, and serve only assets bundled in the package.

## R34 · ubiquitous · risk: security
THE SYSTEM SHALL treat all payer-written and provider-written text (descriptions, references, merchant names, provider categories) as untrusted: escape it in HTML, neutralise leading formula characters in text cells of CSV exports, never send it to a model, and never act on it.

## R35 · event · risk: data
WHEN the underwriter purges a case, THE SYSTEM SHALL delete all the case's files, and SHALL record in a firm-level ledger only the case id, the purge time and who purged it.

## R36 · event · risk: data
WHEN a UK Open Banking (OBIE Account and Transaction API v3.1) transactions file is imported, THE SYSTEM SHALL keep only booked GBP transactions, keep the provider's transaction ids, rebuild the running balance from per-line balances or from a supplied statement balance, and refuse the file if the balance chain breaks anywhere.
Source: D5; D30; E3 and E7 (provider unknown); the reply names TrueLayer, Yapily and Plaid as common.

## R37 · event · risk: data
WHEN a TrueLayer Data API transactions export is imported, THE SYSTEM SHALL apply the same checks as R36, and SHALL keep the provider's own categories only as untrusted hints that no figure uses.
Source: D30.

## R38 · event · risk: data
WHEN a bank CSV with separate paid-in and paid-out columns, a non-ISO date format or newest-first order is imported, THE SYSTEM SHALL convert it through a named bank profile or a custom column mapping, and SHALL apply the same checks as the five-column loader.

## R39 · conditional · risk: data
IF a file already imported into the case is imported again, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL leave the case unchanged.

## R40 · unwanted · risk: data
IF a new account overlaps an existing account of the case in period and shares most of its (date, amount) pairs, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT add it, and SHALL say it is probably the same account imported twice.

## R41 · ubiquitous · risk: money
THE SYSTEM SHALL keep line ids unique within a case by prefixing them with the account key when the case holds more than one account, compute flow figures across all the case's accounts after removing paired own-account transfers, and compute balance figures on the combined end-of-day balance over the dates every account covers, showing n/a with the reason when those dates do not overlap.

## R42 · ubiquitous · risk: data
THE SYSTEM SHALL append every import, profile change, override, firm-rule promotion, preview, pack write and sign-off to the case log, each entry carrying the hash of the entry before it.
Source: the reply, 'The firm would need confidence that data is secure, access is controlled and there's an audit trail.'

## R43 · unwanted · risk: data
IF the case log's hash chain is broken or its last entry is incomplete, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT accept a sign-off, and SHALL name the first bad entry.

## R44 · event · risk: data
WHEN asked to verify an evidence record, THE SYSTEM SHALL recompute every figure, bucket and monthly cell from the recorded inputs and report each mismatch, or confirm that there is none.

## R45 · conditional · risk: data
IF the evidence record was made with a ruleset other than the one installed, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse to verify it, and SHALL name the package version and ruleset that made it.

## R46 · event · risk: data
WHEN asked to pseudonymise a statement, THE SYSTEM SHALL write a copy in which personal and business names and account numbers are replaced by consistent tokens while recognised institutions (acquirers, lenders, HMRC) and all amounts, dates and balances are kept, SHALL tokenise the case profile the same way, and SHALL label the output as pseudonymised personal data, not anonymous data.
Source: the reply, 'I'd start with synthetic or properly anonymised sample statements and compare the results with our existing process'.

## R47 · ubiquitous · risk: none
THE SYSTEM SHALL generate synthetic business cases that include real acquirer names, director funding, own-account transfers across two accounts, cash deposits (at least one at or above the single-deposit limit, and one paid in after a similar cash withdrawal) and lender lines, with ground truth for every bucket, line and indicator, while every existing archetype and profile still produces a byte-identical statement.

## R48 · state · risk: ux
WHILE a case is marked as a demo (synthetic data, or the owner's own statements per D23), THE SYSTEM SHALL show a banner in the workspace and stamp the pack, saying it demonstrates the mechanism and is not an applicant file.

## R50 · event · risk: ux
WHEN asked for a report, THE SYSTEM SHALL summarise for each case the lines in the judgement queue, the lines each indicator flagged, overrides by old and new category, unexplained share of money in, whether every figure was traced, and whether the case was signed off, with no applicant names, descriptions or amounts and no duration derived from the case log's timestamps.
Source: D32 (files are timed with a stopwatch, outside the tool).

## R51 · event · risk: ux
WHEN the underwriter enters their own figure for a memo field or a month, THE SYSTEM SHALL show the difference from its own figure and list, largest first, the lines in that period whose bucket a person might read differently: cash deposits, unexplained lines, possible own-account transfers and overridden lines.
Source: the reply, 'compare the results with our existing process'.

## R52 · event · risk: ux
WHEN the underwriter saves an override on a case of up to 10,000 lines, THE SYSTEM SHALL show the recomputed figures, indicators and policy check within 2 seconds on a typical office laptop.

## R53 · ubiquitous · risk: data
THE SYSTEM SHALL keep cma run, cma resume, cma import monzo, cma generate, the MCP tools and the evidence JSON working with their current options and fields; new evidence fields SHALL be additive, and every new evidence record SHALL carry a schema version.

## R54 · conditional · risk: data
IF CMA_RULESET is set to v1, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL categorise with the built-in rule table as it was before this change, and SHALL record v1 as the ruleset in every evidence record.

## R55 · ubiquitous · risk: money
THE SYSTEM SHALL count every credit categorised as a cash deposit as trading receipts, in M2 and in every figure and monthly cell built on trading receipts, and SHALL report the cash deposits within trading receipts as a separate GBP figure with the ids of the deposits behind it.
Source: D31, 'Counted as trading receipts, with deposits above a threshold flagged'; the reply, 'Highlight ... large cash deposits'.

## R56 · state · risk: ux
WHILE show_policy_verdict is off in the firm configuration, THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT show an overall outcome or any rule result in the review workspace or the pack, and SHALL record in the evidence that the policy check was hidden.
Source: D28 (the setting is the rollback path for showing the outcome).

## P1 · property
For any case, trading receipts and the other seven money-in buckets SHALL sum to total money in to the penny, and every credit's id SHALL appear in exactly one bucket's evidence; the cash-deposits figure is not a bucket and is not added.
Validates: R1, R2, R3, R7

## P2 · property
For any sum figure, bucket or monthly cell, the signed amounts of its evidence lines SHALL total the figure to the penny.
Validates: R1, R11, R16, R55

## P3 · property
For any statements, profile and override log, computing the figures twice SHALL give identical results, and the figures after applying overrides one at a time SHALL equal a fresh computation with all of them applied.
Validates: R17, R44

## P4 · property
For any override log, the set of (id, date, amount, balance, description) across the case's lines SHALL be the same before and after the overrides are applied.
Validates: R18

## P5 · property
For any case whose descriptions and profile contain sentinel strings, no prompt built for a model SHALL contain any sentinel.
Validates: R30, R34

## P6 · property
For any credit that no built-in rule, firm rule or override matches, its id SHALL be in the evidence of unexplained money in and not in the evidence of M2.
Validates: R7

## P7 · property
For any committed synthetic case and test fixture, M1 to M16 under the new ruleset SHALL equal their values before this change, except on lines the change lists as newly recognised; under CMA_RULESET=v1 they SHALL equal them with no exceptions.
Validates: R10, R53, R54

## P8 · property
For any description text, the workspace HTML and the pack HTML SHALL contain it only in escaped form, and no text cell in an exported CSV SHALL begin with =, +, -, @, a tab or a carriage return.
Validates: R34

## P9 · property
For any import file, importing it twice SHALL leave the same case state and the same case log head as importing it once.
Validates: R39

## P10 · property
For any statement and profile, the pseudonymised statement and profile SHALL give identical figures, buckets, monthly cells and indicators.
Validates: R46

## P11 · property
For any multi-account case, each own-account pair SHALL be one debit and one credit of equal amount in different accounts, no line SHALL be in two pairs, and total money in less own-account transfers in SHALL equal the generator's credits from outside the applicant's accounts.
Validates: R6, R8, R9, R41

## P12 · property
For any case, monthly trading receipts SHALL sum to M2 and monthly money in SHALL sum to total money in, to the penny.
Validates: R11, R55

## P13 · property
For any signed pack, verifying its evidence record against its case SHALL reproduce every figure, bucket and monthly cell exactly.
Validates: R22, R44

## P14 · property
For any case, the pack's text SHALL pass the grounding guard with no unmatched numbers and no missing citations.
Validates: R26, R28

## P15 · property
For any case log, changing, removing or reordering any entry before the head SHALL be detected on the next load.
Validates: R42, R43

## P16 · property
For any firm rules file, no line matched by a protected built-in pattern SHALL change category through a firm rule.
Validates: R21

## P17 · property
For any synthetic case generated with the new features, every bucket, every line's category and every indicator flag SHALL equal the generator's ground truth.
Validates: R1, R4, R5, R8, R14, R47, R55

## P18 · property
For any run while offline lock is on, asking for a hosted model or starting the MCP server SHALL fail before any network call is attempted.
Validates: R29

## P19 · property
For any case, the evidence of the cash-deposits figure SHALL be exactly the credits categorised as cash deposits, each of them SHALL also be in M2's evidence, the figure SHALL not exceed M2, and every cash deposit at or above the single-deposit limit SHALL be in the judgement queue with the indicator that flagged it.
Validates: R14, R15, R55

## P20 · property
For any case, with show_policy_verdict on, every workspace panel and pack section that shows a pass, refer or fail outcome SHALL contain the illustrative label and the recommendation field SHALL be empty; with it off, neither the workspace nor the pack SHALL contain an outcome or a rule result.
Validates: R24, R25, R56

# Design — Statement review: every figure traced, the unclear lines first

## Options considered

**Option A: local review workspace (chosen).** The cma package serves a web page on the underwriter's machine, reachable only from that machine (loopback). Every figure, bucket and monthly cell opens its lines, and the lines needing judgement come first. The underwriter re-categorises lines with a reason and the figures layer recomputes, along with the indicators and the illustrative policy check. A named sign-off writes a memo-ready pack and a self-contained HTML record. The model is off by default.

**Option B: static HTML report plus a CLI overrides file.** Each run writes one self-contained HTML file with click-through. Corrections are typed into an overrides file and the run repeated; sign-off stays at the terminal. This is the cheapest option and needs no server. *It lost because* the two things the underwriter asked for beyond click-through, correcting categories and a usable summary, would happen in a file-editing loop outside the page, and the underwriter would see the effect of a correction on the figures and the policy check only after a re-run. It is kept as the format of the signed record (the pack's HTML).

**Option C: spreadsheet as the interface.** Export lines and figures to a workbook, let the underwriter edit a category column, and re-import. It is familiar: they add things up in a spreadsheet today. *It lost because* a figure loses its link to its evidence as soon as a cell is edited or copied. The tool also cannot tell a category correction from an edited amount, and re-importing a hand-edited workbook is the error-prone step the bet is meant to remove. A monthly-summary CSV stays as an export.

**Option D: hosted service (SaaS) now.** One hosted web app per firm; D14 frames the business as SaaS. *It lost for this bet because* applicant data would leave the firm, which is the blocker the reply names. A hosted pilot also needs sign-in, tenancy and a data processing agreement before the approver will look at it. Option A's workspace is the same web page, so hosting it later is a change of deployment, not a rewrite. The owner confirmed local-first (D29).

**Option E: let a model categorise the unclear lines.** Send unexplained lines to a model and accept the buckets it suggests. *It lost because* it puts payer-written text and names in a prompt, which raises GDPR and prompt-injection risk from whoever wrote the payment reference. It also breaks ADR 001 ('the model receives a table, not a statement'), and a category chosen by a model is exactly the kind of invented judgement the underwriter fears. Deterministic rules, rules the firm learns and per-line overrides do this job instead.

**Sub-decision: how to show what is unexplained.** (i) Redefine M16 to mean unexplained only. (ii) Keep M16's value (money in that is not trading receipts), rename it to say so, and add a figure for each bucket plus the unexplained share (M26). *Chose (ii)*: a memo already signed that cites M16 must keep its meaning, and ids are stable.

**Sub-decision: how cash deposits count (D31).** (i) Out of trading receipts until the underwriter moves them (revision 1). (ii) In trading receipts, with the cash inside them reported as its own figure (M18) and indicators on large deposits, cash-heavy months and cash withdrawn then paid back in. (iii) A firm setting that chooses (i) or (ii). *Chose (ii)*, the owner's answer. (i) lost because it understates a cash business such as a café and makes the underwriter add back every ordinary deposit by hand. (iii) lost because M2 would then mean different things in different packs, so a signed memo citing M2 could not be read without knowing the setting; a firm that wants a deposit out moves it with an override and a reason. What (ii) gives up: personal cash paid in by an owner lifts M2, M9 and M10 unless an indicator catches it or a person moves it (see Consequences).

**Sub-decision: how the policy outcome is shown (D28).** (i) Hidden unless the firm loads its own policy (revision 1). (ii) Shown from the packaged policy in the workspace and the pack, with the illustrative label inside the same panel and the same pack section, behind a firm setting that is on by default. (iii) Removed from the review flow; `cma run` keeps it. *Chose (ii)*, the owner's answer. Putting the label in the same section, not in a footnote or only in the HTML record, means copying the section copies the label. (i) lost because the firm has no policy file to load (E8 is open), so the outcome would stay hidden for the whole showcase. (iii) lost because the showcase would no longer show the whole chain, from a traced figure to a rule result that a person must act on.

**Sub-decision: how sign-off works.** (i) Drive the existing LangGraph review interrupt from the workspace. (ii) Make the case folder the source of truth, and make sign-off a case-log event bound to a snapshot hash. *Chose (ii)*. The figures are a pure function of the case's inputs, so a checkpoint would hold nothing extra, and re-running the graph after every override would also re-run the draft node. ReviewDecision's name and notes validation is reused, not copied. `cma run` keeps its interrupt unchanged. Revision 2 settled the order: the underwriter signs a preview, and the pack is written once, at sign-off, from that preview.

**Sub-decision: where the categorisation rules live.** (i) Keep them as code and add more. (ii) Move the rule tables into packaged, validated data files like the policy YAML; the matching passes (reversals, round trips, pairing, profile names) stay in code. *Chose (ii)*: the lists of acquirers, lenders, cash wording and gambling operators are what changes most often, the v1 table can be kept as data for rollback, and a firm's own rules use the same format.

**Sub-decision: how the categoriser settles wording that points two ways (D52, revision 3).** (i) First match in table order, with exceptions inside rules to steer known collisions: v1, and T03's attempts before revision 3. (ii) Two stages, with disagreement as a verdict of its own: line-type cues decide when any match; names decide only when no cue matches; within the deciding stage, matches in two or more buckets make the credit ambiguous. A match inside a longer listed phrase counts only as the longer one, and the bank's own returned-payment code settles the line type alone. (iii) Any two buckets anywhere, cue or name, make the credit ambiguous. *Chose (ii)*. (i) lost because order is a silent choice. Each review round found a new pair of lists it got wrong, and an exception that hides one list's cue when another's is present (HMRC hidden by savings wording) turns a disagreement into a guess nobody sees. (iii) lost because a cue says what the line is and a name says who sent it. Every refund from PayPal, Amazon or an acquirer, and every bounced direct debit to HMRC, would go to the queue though its wording is not in doubt, and it would undo the owner's D46 rule that the cue wins. What (ii) gives up: a cue in payer-written text outranks names, so a payer who writes REFUND moves their credit to refunds. Every cue is non-trading, so this can only understate trading receipts, never invent them. The owner confirmed this reading (D53).

**Sub-decision: what settles an ambiguous credit (revision 3).** (i) Only a per-line override. (ii) A per-line override, a case-profile name or an own-account pairing; never a firm rule. (iii) Anything that ranks above the built-in table's unprotected rules, firm rules included. *Chose (ii)*, which the owner confirmed (D54). (i) contradicts R5, R6 and R8, which say a credit from a director or own account named in the profile, or a paired transfer, SHALL take that category; the owner asked to keep them. Profile names and pairing only ever give non-trading buckets, so R4's rule that an ambiguous credit is never trading receipts holds. (iii) lost because a firm rule can name trading receipts, and it was previewed on another case's lines, not on this one. It would count ambiguous wording as trading without a person looking at the line.

**Sub-decision: what an ambiguous credit records as its candidates (D60, revision 4).** (i) The matches of the stage that decided (revision 3's reading, and T03's fifth attempt). (ii) Every rule the credit matched in either stage, after a match inside a longer phrase counts as the longer one, the payment rail included. *Chose (ii)*, the owner's answer. (i) lost because the underwriter would not see a name that the cues outranked: FPS CREDIT HMRC TO SAVINGS STRIPE would show HMRC and savings and hide the gateway, which is the reason a person might call it trading. What (ii) costs: longer lists, and a rail candidate that gives no bucket, which the queue shows as such.

**Sub-decision: where the judgement queue is required (D60, revision 4).** (i) In R4, so the categoriser's task also had to show the queue (revision 3). (ii) In R15, the case view, whose task builds the queue; R4 requires only what the categoriser produces. (iii) In both R4 and R15. *Chose (ii)*, the owner's answer. (i) lost because T03 could not complete R4 without the workspace, which depends on T03 (the fifth review failed it for that). (iii) lost for the same reason. What (ii) leaves out: `cma run` is not a case and shows no queue; its evidence lines carry the conflict and candidates (Out of scope).

**Sub-decision: which category a credit gets inside one bucket (revision 4).** Two rules can agree on the bucket but carry different categories: a gateway (card settlement) and an invoice reference (customer transfer) are both trading receipts; a returned-payment cue and a refund cue are both refunds and returned payments. The category matters downstream: the round-trip check undoes only customer transfers, M15 reads customer transfers, M7, reversal linking and the returned-DD indicator read returned payments, the M16 numerator reads refunds, and M18 and the cash indicators read cash deposits. (i) The first rule in table order (revision 3): reordering rules then changes M2, M7 and M15, which the fifth review showed. (ii) Make it ambiguous: R4 defines ambiguity by bucket, so this would amend R4 and fill the queue with credits whose bucket is not in doubt. (iii) A category order declared with the table and applied once the bucket is known, putting first the category that brings more checks. *Chose (iii)* as the design default (owner question): in trading receipts, cash deposit, then customer transfer, then card settlement; in refunds and returned payments, returned payment, then refund. A payer cannot avoid the round-trip check by adding a gateway's name, or the cash flags by adding an invoice reference. What (iii) costs: a gateway payout that carries an invoice reference counts as a named customer in M15. The order is data in the table and is hashed with it.

Built-in tables v1 (today's, frozen, first match wins) and v2 (the new lists, in two stages). v2 names cash paid in (counter, deposit machine, Post Office and PayPoint wording) as cash_deposit, and names cash-withdrawal wording that only the cash round-trip indicator reads.   - *Stage 1, line-type cues*: explicit wording of what the line is. A returned payment, a move to or from the applicant's own pot, space or savings, HMRC, a refund or reversal, and the payment rail (Faster Payment, BACS, CHAPS, a bank giro credit, a transfer, a standing order). The rail has no bucket of its own; it says the money did not arrive as cash.
  - *Stage 2, name lists*: who sent the money or what it is for. Cash paid-in wording; lenders and merchant cash advance providers; director, capital-introduced and shareholder wording; generic loan wording; acquirers, gateways, marketplaces and delivery platforms; invoice references; explained non-trading words (interest, grant, cashback, compensation, insurance claim).
  - *Whole words* (revision 4): a listed word or phrase, and a name from the case profile, matches only where the character on each side is not a letter or a digit in any script. CAFÉSTRIPE LTD does not contain STRIPE. The words of a phrase may be separated by any run of spaces. Rules and profile names share this one definition.
  - *The verdict on a credit*, in this order:
    1. Collect every credit rule that matches, from both stages. A match inside a longer match from another rule counts only as the longer one (STRIPE inside STRIPE CAPITAL, LOAN inside DIRECTOR LOAN, REFUND inside HMRC REFUND). What remains are the credit's matches.
    2. A returned-payment code the bank prints at the start of the line settles the line type on its own, because it is the bank's code, not payer wording.
    3. A payment rail together with cash paid-in wording makes the credit ambiguous, whatever other cue matches (BACS CREDIT HMRC CASH PAID IN): the line says both that the money came by transfer and that it came as cash.
    4. Otherwise, if any cue with a bucket matches, the cues decide: cues in one bucket give that bucket, and cues in two or more buckets make the credit ambiguous.
    5. With no such cue, the names decide in the same way. The rail alone decides nothing. If no name matches either, nothing is decided, and the line falls through the precedence below to firm rules and the default.
    6. Inside the bucket decided, the category is the first in the table's declared category order that a deciding match carries: in trading receipts, cash deposit, then customer transfer, then card settlement; in refunds and returned payments, returned payment, then refund. Every other bucket has one category. The rule recorded is the first deciding match, in table order, that carries that category.
    7. An ambiguous credit's candidates are all of its matches from step 1, from both stages and the rail included, written in table order. Its category is other (unexplained).
  - *Bare words are not evidence* (D48): SAVINGS, SAVER, POT, SPACE or a pot label such as TAX POT without move wording, and CAPITAL outside capital introduced, injected or contributed, match no list.
  - *No hidden tie-breaks*: a rule's own exceptions may exclude wording that is on no list (a cheque is not cash), but never another list's cue or name. Where two lists' wording meets, either a longer phrase goes on one list, or the credit is ambiguous.
  - *Precedence*, highest first: (1) a per-line override; (2) a protected verdict, meaning the line-type cues plus lender, director, capital-introduced, shareholder and generic loan wording (R21's patterns and the cues); (3) a case-profile name (R5, R6) or an own-account pairing (R8); (4) an ambiguous verdict, which puts the credit in unexplained money in with every candidate recorded; (5) firm rules, which therefore never reach a line settled at (2) or (4) (R21, R4); (6) an unprotected verdict: the trading lists, invoice references, cash paid in and explained non-trading words; (7) the default, where a debit is supplier and a credit is unexplained.

So the only routes into trading receipts are an unambiguous trading verdict, a firm rule on a line that steps (2) to (4) did not settle, and a person's override.

## Consequences

**Gains**
- The underwriter gets the view they asked for: £80k in, of which £55k is trading and the other £25k is explained by bucket. Every figure is clickable, and their own corrections are on record.
- A cash business is not understated: takings paid in as cash count as trading, the cash inside them is its own figure, and the deposits a person should look at come first (D31).
- No silent choice between lists: when the shipped lists disagree about a credit, the underwriter sees the line, every rule it matched in either stage and the bucket each would give, so a name the cues outranked is still in view (D60). Neither the bucket nor the category depends on the order of rules within a stage, which a test checks by shuffling them and recategorising whole statements (D52, revision 4).
- Each task can now finish its own requirement: T03 delivers R4 through `cma run`'s evidence, and the queue's tasks deliver R15 (D58, D60).
- The showcase runs the whole chain, from traced figures to an illustrative pass, refer or fail that names the rules a person must look at, and the label says whose decision it is (D28).
- The approver's question, does data leave the firm, has an answer the code enforces: offline lock on, the MCP server refuses to start, and the evidence states offline mode.
- Firm rules build up in a file the firm owns. That is the only switching cost any board lens found.
- The bet's outcome is read by stopwatch on comparable files (D32). For each case, the report adds the size of the judgement queue, the indicator counts and the overrides by kind. Those explain the minutes without the tool measuring the person.

**Costs and risks**
- The scope is large for two weeks and $20, and Tier 1 alone is most of it. T03 has used its five attempts and needs re-opening on revision 4's R4; its scope is now the categoriser alone.
- A server, even one reachable only from the same machine, is new attack surface (see Security notes).
- Twelve more figures make the `cma run` prompt longer and the appendix wider.
- Cash paid in by the owner now counts as trading receipts. It lifts M2, M9 and M10, and can turn an illustrative fail into a pass (D31). The single-deposit, monthly-share and round-trip indicators catch the common patterns. They miss personal cash split into deposits below the limit, in months where cash stays under the share limit. The underwriter sees that only in M18 and the cash lines.
- More lines in the judgement queue (D52). A genuine cash deposit at a branch whose name holds a listed word, or a card settlement whose reference names a lender, sits in unexplained money in, outside M2, M9 and M18, until the underwriter moves it. The policy can understate trading receipts; it never overstates them.
- Longer candidate lists (D60). An ambiguous credit lists every rule it matched in either stage, the rail among them. A candidate's bucket can be one the deciding stage outranked, such as trading receipts for a gateway name beside two disagreeing cues; it is shown so the underwriter can choose it, never counted.
- The category order inside a bucket (revision 4) sends a gateway payout that carries an invoice reference through the round-trip check and counts it as a named customer in M15, and counts a line with both returned-payment and refund wording as a returned direct debit in M7. Both lean toward more checks, and both are one list in the table.
- Payer-written cues move credits: a payer who writes REFUND or TO SAVINGS in a reference takes their credit out of trading receipts or into the queue. Every cue is non-trading, so this can only lower M2.
- An outcome on screen can be read as the tool deciding. The friend said they don't want that, and the approver may object to it. The label sits beside every outcome, the recommendation stays blank, and show_policy_verdict turns the outcome off without a release.
- On the owner's own statements the illustrative policy will probably refer or fail, because a personal account has little trading income. The demo banner (R48) says the case demonstrates the mechanism; the presenter should say why before showing it.
- The categoriser still reads payer-written text, and a payer can name themselves after an acquirer. Indicators reduce this but do not remove it.
- The requirement most likely to be wrong is that the reply's 13 generic fields are the firm's memo. It is cheap to check (E8: a redacted template) and cheap to fix, because the field map is data. Next most likely: the cash default (D31) and its limits (D35), which rest on one anecdotal source; and the category order inside a bucket, new in revision 4 and put to the owner, which is one list in the table.

### Perspective check

- **Security.** *Who can call it:* the operating-system user who owns the case root. The workspace also needs a per-launch token and a loopback Host header (R33). *Trust boundary:* imported files and payer text are checked by the loader and escaped on output (R34). *Secrets:* only an optional model key in the environment, never logged. *Personal data:* kept under one case root readable only by its owner, never committed to git (R31), never in prompts (R30); evidence holds only hashes of the profile. *Risk path:* lending data; the human acknowledgement is the named sign-off bound to a snapshot that includes the policy hash and whether the check was shown (R22). The illustrative outcome is not an acknowledgement. *Worst case:* see Security notes, now including cash paid in to look like trading, wording that mixes lists, and a listed name hidden inside a longer word.
- **Platform.** *Blast radius:* one Python package; new optional parts; the evidence JSON gains fields; PolicyResult and the checkpoint allow-list do not change. *Old and new side by side:* `cma run` is untouched, new commands are additive, and CMA_RULESET=v1 reproduces today's categories, cash included, with first-match order and no ambiguity verdict. *Resources:* files on disk only; no tables, queues, cron jobs or IAM. *Rollback:* an environment flag (CMA_RULESET), a config flip (show_policy_verdict) or a reinstall, with no data repair. *Observability:* see that section.
- **Staff.** *Smallest change:* Tier 1 is the smallest set that shows the mechanism in the reply's terms; Tier 2 can be cut off. The cash change is one category mapped into an existing set, and the policy check reuses policy.evaluate and the guard as they are. The ambiguity policy replaces per-pair exceptions with one verdict and keeps revision 2's precedence, inserting that verdict between the profile and firm rules. Revision 4 makes R4 smaller: the queue it named belongs to R15. *Ownership:* arithmetic and the queue's assembly stay in metrics.py and indicators.py, the outcome in policy.py, categorisation in categorise.py plus the rule data; the workspace and pack only render. *Six-month misunderstandings removed:* M16 is renamed so it cannot be confused with M26 (unexplained); M18 is the cash inside M2, not a bucket beside it; [R1] to [R9] in a pack are policy rules, not requirement ids; the action reads 'sign off figures', not 'approve the loan'; OTHER means unexplained; an ambiguous credit is unexplained because the lists disagree, not because nothing matched, and its rule says conflict and names every rule it matched in either stage, not only the stage that decided; the category inside a bucket comes from the table's declared order, not rule order; pseudonymised data is still personal data. *Most likely wrong:* the memo fields (E8), the cash default (D31) and limits (D35), and the category order inside a bucket. *Out of scope:* listed above.
- **Clean code.** *What changes most:* the rule lists, the category order and the thresholds, kept apart as data. *Names:* follow the code: money in (inflows in metrics.py), trading receipts (M2 keeps its name, Total revenue, so signed memos still read), override, firm rule, case, preview, pack, sign-off, policy check, line-type cue, name list, conflict, candidates. *Tests:* properties P1-P20, synthetic truth for every bucket and indicator, golden files for the importers, a pairwise matrix over every two credit rules, and a shuffle test on rule order within each stage that recategorises whole statements and compares categories and figures. *Duplication removed:* all importers share one balance walk; sign-off reuses ReviewDecision's validation; the pack's policy section reuses policy.evaluate and the guard's [Rn] check; exceptions that steer one list away from another give way to one verdict and longer phrases; rules and profile names share one whole-word definition. *Duplication introduced:* the v1 rule table, kept as data for one release. *No single-caller abstraction:* no storage interface for a future hosted version; the label is one constant, not a templating layer; the importer contract has four callers; the rule-to-category lookup the queue uses is the table itself.
- **Data-intensive.** *Idempotency:* imports are keyed by file hash, an identical override changes nothing, and a second sign-off is refused. *Determinism:* a credit's verdict, category and candidates are a pure function of its description, the sign of its amount and the tables with their category order; neither bucket nor category depends on rule order within a stage, and only which of several same-category rules is recorded, and the order candidates are written in, follow table order. *Ordering and concurrency:* one writer per case, enforced by a lock plus the expected log position; a second tab gets a conflict and reloads. *Partial failure:* append-only logs with a check for a torn last entry; the pack is written to a temporary folder and then renamed. *Consistency:* the workspace reads the latest state; the preview and sign-off bind to a snapshot that includes the ruleset, thresholds, the policy hash and the show_policy_verdict setting, so a sign-off cannot attach to an outcome the underwriter did not see. *Migration:* additive, nothing to backfill. *Money:* integer pence, GBP only, thresholds compared in pence, and amounts with more than two decimals are refused.

**Monthly summary.** One row per calendar month: the month, a part-month flag, money in, money out, trading receipts (cash included), average and lowest end-of-day balance, and days overdrawn. Each cell carries its evidence ids and their total.

**Judgement queue.** One entry per line, built by C2 and read by C5 and `cma report`: the line id, the reason it is listed (unexplained, ambiguous, possible own-account transfer, or the indicators that flagged it), and for an ambiguous credit its candidates, each with its rule id, the category that rule sets and the bucket that category maps to (none for the rail). Ordered by amount, largest first. It holds no money arithmetic.

**Indicators.** Each has an id, a kind, the threshold that fired, evidence ids and a one-line reason. Thresholds live in a packaged, validated YAML file that the firm can replace. Amounts in it are pounds with at most two decimals and are compared in pence. While a threshold still has its shipped value, the workspace and the pack call it illustrative, as they do the policy. Kinds: a large single credit against typical trading receipts; a cash deposit at or above the single-deposit limit; a month with cash above a set share of its trading receipts; cash paid in within a window of days after a cash withdrawal, the two amounts within a tolerance; a payment to a gambling operator; a returned direct debit; a run of consecutive overdrawn days; an irregular credit from a named acquirer, read from the acquirer and gateway name lists whatever category the line took. Shipped cash values: a single deposit of £2,500 or more and cash above 50% of a month's trading receipts (D35), and a round trip within 7 days and 10% of the amount (design default). An ambiguous credit is not categorised as cash, so the cash indicators do not read it; it is in the judgement queue as unexplained.

**Policy check.** PolicyResult and policy.evaluate do not change. The workspace and the pack evaluate only the packaged policy. The label is one constant with no digits in it, so it never trips the guard: 'Illustrative thresholds shipped with this tool. They are not your firm's lending policy, and this is not a lending decision: the underwriter decides.' The pack's evidence records whether the check was shown, the label, and the policy's name and hash. These do not go into PolicyResult, so the checkpoint allow-list and `cma run` are untouched. As in revision 1, the description of policy rule R9 is reworded for M16's new name, and the policy hash changes.

**Rule tables.** Packaged YAML under src/cma/rules/. v1 is today's table, frozen and pinned by hash. v2 adds acquirers, gateways, marketplaces and delivery platforms; lenders and merchant cash advance providers; move wording for own pots, spaces and savings; cash paid in (counter, deposit machine, Post Office and PayPoint); cash-withdrawal wording for the round-trip indicator only; HMRC repayments; refunds; explained non-trading credits; and the payment rail as a cue with no category. Every v2 rule carries a stage (line_type or names) and whether it is protected, and line-type rules come before names. Protected in v2: the line-type cues, and lender, director, capital-introduced, shareholder and generic loan wording. Not protected: cash paid in, the trading lists, invoice references and explained non-trading words. Compound wording lives as longer phrases on one list (STRIPE CAPITAL with the lenders, DIRECTOR LOAN with the director wording, HMRC REFUND with HMRC), not as exceptions in another list. Bare pot or savings labels and bare CAPITAL are on no list (D48). v2 also declares its category order inside each bucket that has more than one category (C1, step 6); the order is part of the table and of its hash. ## Interfaces and contracts

**CLI (all additions)**
- `cma case new [--demo] [--label TEXT]` prints a random case id.
- `cma case import CASE FILE --format csv|monzo|openbanking|truelayer|bank-csv[:PROFILE] [--account KEY] [--statement-balance AMOUNT --at DATE]`
- `cma case profile CASE` edits the profile.
- `cma review CASE` starts the workspace, prints the URL with its token, and opens a browser if there is one.
- `cma case preview CASE` prints the memo sections, the policy check when it is shown, and the snapshot hash. It writes nothing.
- `cma case sign CASE` asks for a typed name, checks the snapshot against the preview and writes the pack once. It is interactive only; there is no --yes. Preview and sign-off are also available in the workspace.
- `cma case purge CASE`
- `cma verify EVIDENCE [--case CASE]`
- `cma pseudonymise FILE --format F --out PATH [--profile CASE]`
- `cma report` prints a summary of every case with no personal data and no durations.
- `cma generate` gains opt-in features: director funding, own-account transfers, cash (with large deposits and a round trip), real acquirers, lenders, two accounts.
- Environment variables: CMA_HOME (case root) and CMA_RULESET (v1 or v2).

**Importer contract.** Input: one source file and an optional statement balance. Output: the five-column statement for one account, the account metadata, and an optional hints file. The output must pass ingest.load_csv unchanged, and all importers share one step that walks and verifies the balance. Refusals give line or record numbers, never cell values, as the MCP server does today.

**Review workspace API.** Internal to the package; the page and the server ship together, so it is not a shared contract. It can read the case summary and the judgement queue; read the lines behind a figure, bucket, monthly cell or indicator; read the policy check when it is shown; post an override with the expected log position; preview and promote a firm rule; build a preview; sign off a preview's snapshot; and post a comparison figure. A line in the judgement queue carries its rule and, for an ambiguous credit, its candidates, each with the category its rule sets and the bucket that category maps to, or no bucket for the rail (R15). A line in a drill-down carries its rule as recorded (R16). The firm-rule preview counts the lines the rule matches and will not apply to, because a protected or ambiguous verdict settled them (R20, R21, R4). Every request carries the session token. Every write carries the expected log position and gets a conflict if that position is stale.

**Pack.** memo.md has the sections in field-map order, figures with their ids, and blanks left for the underwriter. While the check is shown, it then has a 'Policy check (illustrative)' section that no memo field maps to. Its first line is the label, followed by the overall outcome and each rule, with the metric value tagged [Mn] and the threshold tagged [Rn] after a limit word. record.html is self-contained and makes no external requests; it shows the label wherever an outcome appears, and shows the sign-off. The pack also holds evidence.json (v1) and monthly.csv. It is written once, at sign-off, to a new folder named by the snapshot hash.

**Memo field map.** A YAML file giving, for each field, its name, the figures or tables it shows, and a sentence template whose numbers are placeholders for figure ids. Fields with nothing mapped are marked for the underwriter. The default reproduces the 13 fields in the reply: business details, loan request, trading history, monthly turnover and credits, average and minimum balances, existing commitments, returned direct debits, VAT and HMRC, director loans and transfers between the business's accounts, credit history, affordability, key risks and recommendation. The turnover field states the cash within trading receipts (M18) next to M2. Credit history, key risks and recommendation stay blank. The policy check is not a memo field; the recommendation stays blank whatever the outcome.

**MCP tools.** compute_metrics returns M1-M28 (an addition), and a new read-only tool returns the money-in buckets. check_policy is unchanged. The server refuses to start under the offline lock.

**Graph and prompt.** Unchanged, except that the metrics table has more rows and M16 has its new name. FakeLLM parses rows by id and is unaffected; its sentence about M16 is reworded. Under v2 the evidence lines `cma run` writes carry each line's rule, the conflict form included; the terminal review shows no queue.

|---|---|---|
| The same file is imported twice | Same hash: the case is unchanged; the log notes it was already imported | R39 |
| The same account arrives as a CSV and as Open Banking JSON, with different ids | Periods overlap and most (date, amount) pairs match: the second is refused as probably the same account | R40 |
| Open Banking JSON has no per-line balances and no statement balance was given | Refused, saying which balance to supply | R36 |
| A paged Open Banking export repeats a transaction id | Identical content: kept once. Different content: refused | R36, R39 |
| The feed includes pending transactions | Left out, and counted in the import message | R36 |
| An account or line is not in GBP | The account is refused; lines are never converted | R36, R2 |
| Lines with equal timestamps cannot be ordered so that the balance chain holds | Refused, naming the first break | R36 |
| Two equal-amount credits could pair with one own-account debit | Not paired; all listed for judgement | R9 |
| A firm rule pattern matches far more lines than expected | The preview shows how many lines in the open case it matches before saving | R20 |
| A credit's line-type cues point to two buckets (an HMRC credit whose reference says TO SAVINGS; a refund from a merchant whose name says SAVINGS TRANSFER) | Ambiguous: unexplained money in, with every rule it matched in either stage recorded as candidates; the judgement queue lists it with each candidate's bucket; never trading receipts unless the underwriter moves it | R4, R15 |
| The cues disagree and a name from a third bucket also matches (FPS CREDIT HMRC TO SAVINGS STRIPE) | Ambiguous; the candidates are the savings move, HMRC, the rail and the gateway, so the queue shows trading receipts as one reading and no bucket for the rail | R4, R15 |
| A credit with no cue matches names in two buckets (COUNTER DEPOSIT at a branch whose name holds INSURANCE CLAIM or a lender's name; cash wording with DIRECTOR) | Ambiguous, as above. A genuine cash deposit waits in the queue, outside M2 and M18, until the underwriter moves it | R4, R15, R55 |
| A payment rail appears with cash paid-in wording (FPS CREDIT ... CASH DEPOSIT), with or without another cue (BACS CREDIT HMRC CASH PAID IN) | Ambiguous whatever other cue matches: the rail says the money did not arrive as cash. The candidates include the rail, the cash wording and any other cue | R4 |
| A credit has one cue and names from another bucket (PAYPAL REFUND, AMAZON REFUND) | The cue decides: refunds. Every cue is non-trading | R4 |

## Observability

Nothing leaves the machine, so every signal is local, and the underwriter chooses whether to share it.

- **The signal that proves it works:** for each case, in `cma report` and in each pack's evidence: traced figures 100% (every figure has evidence or an n/a reason), reconciled true, guard grounded true.
- **The signal that tests the bet's biggest risk:** M26 (unexplained share of money in) on each real or pseudonymised case, and the size of the judgement queue. If most cases sit above 20%, the tool is handing the hard part back (board risk 1).
- **The signal that tests the ambiguity policy (D52, D60):** per case, the number of ambiguous credits, their share of money in, and their candidate sets, read from line provenance in each pack's evidence and counted among the judgement-queue lines in `cma report`. A candidate set that keeps recurring, and that the underwriter keeps moving the same way, needs a longer phrase on one list, not a rule order.
- **The signal that tests the category order (revision 4):** overrides between two categories of the same bucket (customer transfer to card settlement, returned payment to refund), counted by kind in `cma report`. If the friend keeps reversing the order's choice, the order is wrong.
- **The signal that tests D31:** overrides from cash_deposit to another category, and cash deposits flagged, per case, in `cma report`. If the friend moves most flagged cash out of trading receipts, the default or the limits are wrong.
- **The signal for the outcome:** stopwatch minutes per file, recorded by the friend on the trial sheet outside the tool (D32). The case log keeps event times for the audit trail only, and nothing reports a duration from them.
- **Log lines:** one structured line per event in the case log, with the event, case id, snapshot and counts, and no names or descriptions. For example: event=pack_written traced=100 reconciled=true unexplained_pct=12.4 ambiguous=4 cash_flagged=3 policy_check=shown.
- **What fires when it does not work:** there is no remote alerting, by design. Instead the tool refuses, with a non-zero exit and a red banner, when reconciliation fails, the guard fails, the log chain breaks, or a hosted model is requested under the offline lock. `cma report` exits non-zero if any case has traced figures below 100% or reconciled false.
- **CI:** evals extended with truth for every bucket and indicator, the cash ones included; P1-P20 run as tests, with the pairwise matrix and the rule-order shuffle over whole statements; the wheel check also loads the rule tables, thresholds, field map and packaged policy from an installed wheel.

## Security notes

- **Who can call it:** the operating-system user who owns the case root, whose files are readable by that user only. The workspace listens only on loopback, requires a random per-launch token on every request, rejects any Host header that is not the loopback address (against DNS rebinding) and sends no permissive CORS headers. Writes also need the expected log position.
- **Trust boundary:** bank data the applicant controls enters through the importers, and the loader checks its structure and balance chain. Descriptions are written by payers: they are escaped in HTML under a strict content security policy with no inline script, formula characters are neutralised in CSV, and they never go into prompts. The candidate rule ids shown for an ambiguous credit, and their buckets, come from the shipped tables, not from payer text.
- **Secrets:** an optional model API key in the environment, only when the offline lock is off. It is never logged or written to evidence.
- **Personal data:** statements, the profile (director names, account identifiers), override reasons and packs stay in the case folder. Evidence holds ids, figures, rule ids and hashes, not descriptions or the profile. Purge deletes the folder and leaves a ledger line with no personal data. Encryption at rest is the firm's disk encryption; the tool adds none of its own. Retention follows the firm's policy, and purge is how the tool carries it out.
- **Risk path:** lending data (risk: data). The human acknowledgement is the named sign-off bound to the snapshot. The name is typed, not authenticated (README known limit), so the OS user is recorded alongside it. Real sign-in belongs to a hosted version. The illustrative outcome is computed, labelled and never signed as a decision.
- **Worst cases with this deployed:** First, an applicant writes script into a payment reference to act in the underwriter's browser, for example to change categories or sign off. Escaping, the content security policy and the token stop it. Second, an applicant makes money look like trading income: by naming the payer after an acquirer, adding an invoice reference, or, since D31, paying cash in. The round-trip check, the director-name rule and the indicators surface it, including the three cash indicators, and the line is one click from its figure. Cash split below every limit is the gap that remains, and it is visible only in M18. Since D52, wording that mixes lists cannot reach trading receipts: a payer who adds a second list's word only sends the credit to the queue, and every line-type cue is non-trading, so payer-written cues can lower M2 but never raise it. Since revision 4, a listed name hidden inside a longer word in any alphabet does not match, and adding a gateway's name to an invoice-referenced credit does not take it out of the round-trip check. Third, someone turns the offline lock off and uses a hosted model. The prompt still carries only tables (P5), and the evidence records where data went.
- **Pseudonymised is not anonymous:** amounts, dates and balances can identify a business again, so the output is labelled as personal data.
